work.title: The Second Part of King Henry the Sixth

scene.label: Act 4, Scene 3
scene.title: SCENE III. Another part of Blackheath

content.text: [Alarums to the fight, wherein both the Staffords are slain. Enter Cade and the rest.

lines.text: Where's Dick, the butcher of Ashford?
lines.plainText: Where's Dick the butcher of Ashford

lines.text: They fell before thee like sheep and oxen, and thou behaved'st thyself as if thou hadst been in thine own slaughterhouse. Therefore thus will I reward thee: the Lent shall be as long again as it is, and thou shalt have a licence to kill for a hundred lacking one.
lines.plainText: They fell before thee like sheep and oxen and thou behaved'st thyself as if thou hadst been in thine own slaughterhouse Therefore thus will I reward thee the Lent shall be as long again as it is and thou shalt have a licence to kill for a hundred lacking one

lines.text: And, to speak truth, thou deservest no less. This monument of the victory will I bear. [putting on Sir Humphrey's brigandine] And the bodies shall be dragged at my horse heels till I do come to London, where we will have the Mayor's sword borne before us.
lines.plainText: And to speak truth thou deservest no less This monument of the victory will I bear putting on Sir Humphrey's brigandine And the bodies shall be dragged at my horse heels till I do come to London where we will have the Mayor's sword borne before us

lines.text: If we mean to thrive and do good, break open the gaols and let out the prisoners.
lines.plainText: If we mean to thrive and do good break open the gaols and let out the prisoners

lines.text: Fear not that, I warrant thee. Come, let's march towards London.
lines.plainText: Fear not that I warrant thee Come let's march towards London
